definition: Set of technologies dedicated to the design, programming, and use of robots to automate tasks, improve precision, safety, and efficiency of industrial processes.

Manufacturing and assembly techniques for product parts or components, including various methods (welding, bonding, machining, etc.) aimed at ensuring quality, reliability, and performance of finished products.
Production method that creates objects by adding material layer by layer from a 3D digital model. It enables production of complex, custom parts with less waste than traditional methods.

Techniques and tools to monitor the real-time state of a structure or industrial process using sensors and data acquisition systems, combined with analysis tools to detect anomalies, anticipate failures, or optimize performance.

Development of adaptable and responsive production systems capable of quickly changing manufactured products, processes, or volumes to meet fluctuating market needs, custom demands, and technological evolution.

Design approach that integrates environmental impacts from the early stages of product or service development to reduce its ecological footprint throughout its lifecycle (from raw material extraction to recycling).
Optimization of industrial processes to reduce emissions, energy, and resource consumption, potentially incorporating circular economy principles and green chemistry.

sub_domain: Waste and Effluent Reduction and Treatment
definition: Methods aimed at reducing the amount of liquid, solid, or gaseous waste generated by industrial activities and treating it to limit environmental and human health impact.
Practices that extend the life of materials, components, or products by transforming, repairing, or reusing them within a circular economy logic and waste reduction.
Transition to low-greenhouse-gas-emission transport modes (land, air, sea) via electrification, alternative fuels, or energy optimization of vehicles and infrastructure.
Reduction of CO2 emissions related to energy production and consumption through renewable energy development, improved energy efficiency, and substitution of fossil fuels.

Development and use of innovative materials (composites, bio-based materials, nanomaterials, etc.) with specific properties (lightweight, strength, durability), adapted to industrial performance and sustainability requirements.
Use of algorithms and computational models that enable machines to perform tasks requiring human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, perception, and decision-making in industrial contexts.

Deployment of interconnected production environments where equipment, systems, and operators exchange real-time data via digital technologies (IoT, sensors, cloud, AI, etc.), improving performance through continuous monitoring, predictive maintenance, traceability, and adaptability.

sub_domain: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes
definition: Use of digital tools (CAD, simulation, digital twins, etc.) to design, model, test, and improve products and manufacturing processes from concept to production, reducing development cycles and increasing reliability.

Ability of a company to achieve objectives in quality, cost, time, flexibility, and innovation through coordinated use of continuous improvement methods, performance indicators, integrated digital tools (e.g., ERP), and process optimization.

Actions, training, and systems implemented to support the evolution of skills and professional profiles required in Industry 4.0, including anticipation of skill needs and adaptation to emerging technologies (AI, robotics, data, etc.).

Process of supporting individuals, teams, and organizations in transitioning to new practices, tools, or models, aiming to reduce resistance and ensure sustainable adoption of technological and organizational changes.
Design approach that places the needs, expectations, and constraints of end users at the center of product, service, or system development, improving usability, ergonomics, and user satisfaction.
Integration of technologies (augmented reality, cobots, artificial intelligence, etc.) to enhance physical, cognitive, or decision-making capabilities of operators in industrial environments.

Set of activities, methods, and technologies aimed at transmitting knowledge, skills, and experience, and effectively training individuals or teams to improve organizational performance and adaptability.
